key_insight: Adding patient-reported outcomes to surrogate endpoints improved machine learning prediction of trial-level overall survival benefit, increasing AUC-ROC from 0.67 to 0.79.
clinical_relevance: Combining patients’ reported experiences with efficacy endpoints may strengthen assessment of survival benefit in oncology drug development.
method: Reviewed trials supporting FDA oncology drug approvals from 2013–2023.
Compared models using surrogate endpoints alone versus surrogate endpoints plus patient-reported outcomes.
Evaluated performance with repeated five-fold trial-grouped cross-validation and leave-one-trial-out validation.
evidence_signal: Across 100 trials, 103 between-arm comparisons, and 68,987 participants, leave-one-trial-out validation showed an AUC-ROC increase of 0.132 (95% CI, 0.017–0.248).
watch_item: Validation was internal to selected approval-supporting trials; generalizability to other settings and use as a substitute for observed survival remain unestablished.
paper_title: Improving Survival Prediction from Surrogate Endpoints Through Integration of Patient-Reported Outcomes Using Machine Learning
